headline: You refine frontend interfaces through precise corrections, accessible interactions, and pragmatic compromises—often after midnight.

archetype.name: The Midnight Interface Tuner
archetype.description: You work in short, concrete steps: adjust the layout, check the behavior, then add another layer of polish. Your prompts connect visual details with keyboard access, browser behavior, and loading costs. You give the assistant specific technical direction, while accepting practical fallbacks when a fix keeps resisting.

dimensions.title: Small steps, concrete checks
dimensions.summary: You often refine results through focused follow-ups, adding requirements as the implementation takes shape. When browser behavior or asset costs get in the way, you sometimes choose a workable fallback and defer the harder fix.

dimensions.title: Brief and technically specific
dimensions.summary: You usually write concise Traditional Chinese with English technical terms embedded naturally. Your corrections often identify the exact mismatch and name the implementation change you want.

dimensions.title: Frontend implementation fluency
dimensions.summary: Your requests show familiarity with CSS layout, React hooks, validation, component tooling, and browser APIs. You also bring specific hypotheses to debugging; in one performance session, you challenged the image-loading diagnosis and proposed a concrete change.

dimensions.title: Polish that stays usable
dimensions.summary: You repeatedly ask for accessibility details alongside visual and interaction refinements. Contrast, reduced motion, error focus, keyboard controls, and touch targets appear across different sessions. You also care about subtle feedback, from skeleton loading to restrained shadows and badge animation.

dimensions.title: Visible next steps
dimensions.summary: Your prompts show requests for more reusable UI foundations, including design tokens, component variants, and stories. They also leave a specific loose end: in one session, you deferred a Next.js Image export issue after choosing native img. These are visible directions and unfinished work, rather than evidence of completed improvements.

traits.name: Accessibility stays in the details
traits.description: You repeatedly bring accessibility into concrete implementation requests, including accessible names, motion preferences, touch targets, and focus styling.

traits.name: Precise feedback loop
traits.description: You often steer the assistant with small, testable corrections, specifying values or behavior instead of leaving the desired change vague.

traits.name: Pragmatic fallback chooser
traits.description: Across several sessions, you accept simpler alternatives when repeated failures or loading costs make the original approach less useful.

traits.name: Interaction detail tuner
traits.description: You often continue past basic functionality to refine loading feedback, shadow weight, and animation behavior.

traits.description: In a few sessions, you ask to move UI decisions into reusable structures, from named color tokens to component variants and supporting stories.
